title: Marathon Essentials — official guide (insurance boundary, medical escort, weather, luggage, inclusions/exclusions)
publisher: Tenzing Hillary Everest Marathon (event organiser, Kathmandu)
claims: All members require travel or medical insurance from their own respective countries; international travel, trip cancellation and medical insurance, and emergency evacuation or medical costs are listed as package exclusions.
Doctors accompany the group to Everest Base Camp and back to Lukla; helicopters are available on extra payment for evacuation to the nearest facility or to a Kathmandu hospital.
The page quotes a guideline one-way helicopter cost of about USD 600 per person when the helicopter is full (five people); this is a general guideline figure, not the race-day evacuation tariff.
High-altitude advice on the page: do not take sleeping pills at higher altitude; carry personal medication and consult the accompanying doctor or guide before taking pills.

May weather description: daytime 10–20°C, morning and night -5 to -10°C depending on altitude and wind chill; strong UV above 3,400 m with SPF 30–50 sunscreen; starry nights -2 to -8°C; snow of 1–2 ft is possible.
Luggage allowance is 15 kg / 30 lb; excess domestic flight luggage is charged USD 1.2 per kg; the pre-race briefing is held at Hotel Shanker on 17 May.

Package inclusions: 4 nights twin B&B in Kathmandu, airport transfers, fixed-wing domestic flight Kathmandu–Lukla–Kathmandu or Ramechhap–Lukla–Ramechhap (excluding emergency/medical evacuation or change to helicopter), full board during the trek, permits and park fees, half-day Kathmandu sightseeing, event t-shirt, medal, certificate, souvenir and the 2 June celebration dinner.

Package exclusions: Nepal visa (USD 50 for 30 days or USD 30 for 15 days), international flights, Kathmandu meals, personal expenses, international travel/trip cancellation/medical insurance, emergency evacuation or medical costs, and any extra early departure.
